newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH O/N DEPOS CLOSE TO LOMBARD, ZLOTY JUST UP.
newsitem.headline: POLISH O/N DEPOS CLOSE TO LOMBARD, ZLOTY JUST UP.

text.p: The Polish money market remained dry throughout the day as most players searched for overnight cash to square positions on the last day of October's reserve, dealers said.

They said rates were close to the central bank's lombard rate of 25 percent and there were still many players willing to buy O/N cash, but that the market would likely become more liquid on Thursday - first day of new reserve period.
"Rates were close to the lombard rate and traders still wanted to buy, but the situation is likely normalise tomorrow on the new reserve period," said Monika Gradowska from BIG SA.
Overnight rates were quoted at 24.95/25.20 percent against the opening's 24.80/25.10 percent. Tomorrow/next were at 19.80/20.30 percent versus 19.50/20.50 percent.

Dealers expected O/N prices fall to some 19.75 percent tomorrow. Interbank one-month repo deals done today with spot value date at 19.28 percent also signalled liquidity may improve. High interbank rates stifled turnover on the secondary T-bill market. Yields went up as banks were reluctant to buy treasuries amid a general cash shortage.
"Expensive short term money kills secondary T-bill trade," said Piotr Czyzewski from ING Bank.
Dealers also said that T-bill yields were not likely to fall in the near-term because they mirrored a recent yield growth trend at the weekly primary tenders.

The benchmark 52-week paper's maximum yield rose 0.03 point to 19.50 percent at Monday's primary sale, and it was quoted at 19.52/44 percent on Wednesday. The zloty's light trade session reflected international dollar moves. It closed at 1.93/1.88 percent from the parity rate, a touch stronger than Tuesday's close at 1.91/1.86. It closed at 2.8110/30 to the dollar, down from 2.8091/01 on Tuesday and at 1.8605/15 to the mark against 1.8606/18. -- Krzysztof Wojcik +48 22 653 9700
